Declarative Logger Configuration

Source: R/config.R
config.Rd

lgr can be configured from a single canonical, versioned configuration format (version: 1) that can express the entire logger hierarchy: the root logger, descendant loggers, and reusable named layouts, filters and appenders. Use Logger$config() (usually via lgr$config()) to apply such a config, or read_config()/validate_config() to check a config without applying it.

Top-level structure

A config document is a mapping with an optional version (defaults to 1; no other value is currently supported), an optional disable_existing_loggers flag, and the optional sections layouts, filters, appenders and loggers. loggers is a mapping from logger name (root for the root logger, /-separated names such as app/db for descendants) to a logger definition supporting class ("Logger" or "LoggerGlue"), threshold, appenders, filters, propagate and exception_handler. layouts/filters/appenders are mappings from a user-chosen component name to a component definition: a mapping with a class key (e.g. class: AppenderConsole, optionally namespaced as pkg::ClassName) plus the remaining keys as constructor arguments. Component names can be referenced by name wherever a layouts/filters/ appenders value is expected (in another component, or in a logger); such references are resolved once and the resulting object is shared. Appenders and filters can also be defined inline instead of referenced by name.

Function-valued positions (a logger's exception_handler, and filter entries) accept one of: a name reference (a bare character scalar for exception_handler, or an explicit { ref: <name> }), resolved by lookup (<pkg>::<name> supported); an inline code form ({ code: "<R source>" }), the only form that evaluates config-supplied source and is therefore rejected unless the loader is called with allow_code = TRUE; and, for filters only, a { class: <FilterClass>, ... } spec (constructing an R6 EventFilter) or a bare-string reference to a named filters component.

Applying a config is a full snapshot, not a patch

A logger definition under loggers fully determines that logger's threshold, appenders, filters, propagate and exception_handler: any of these keys that are not given for a listed logger are reset to their default (no threshold/inherited, no appenders, no filters, propagate: true, the default exception handler) rather than left as they were before the config was applied. This makes re-applying the same declarative config (or switching between config files) reproducible and independent of whatever state a Logger happened to be in beforehand. Note that this differs from the plain (non-declarative) list form accepted by Logger$config(), which only touches the elements it is given and leaves everything else untouched.

disable_existing_loggers

If TRUE, every pre-existing non-root logger not named under loggers is reset to its default/unconfigured state before the rest of the config is applied (loggers that are named under loggers are unaffected by this flag; they always end up in the state the config describes for them, per the previous section). Defaults to FALSE, so orphaned loggers are left alone unless you opt in.

Resetting is not the same as silencing. A reset logger gets propagate = TRUE and no appenders/threshold of its own, i.e. it now inherits its ancestors' appenders and threshold. If a logger was deliberately muted (e.g. propagate: false with no appenders) before the reset, this can make it more verbose afterwards, not less – it starts forwarding events to whichever ancestor appenders it now inherits from.

Environment variable interpolation

Scalar string values may contain ${VAR} (substituted with the value of environment variable VAR) or ${VAR:-default} (using default when VAR is unset or empty). A literal ${...} can be produced with the escape $${...}. A value produced entirely by interpolation is leniently coerced (number-like to numeric, true/false to logical), so size: ${SIZE} behaves like a literal size: 1048576. Interpolation happens before validation and is never applied to code: payloads.

Safety

Loading a config never evaluates config-supplied R source by default. Only the code: form does so, and it is rejected during validation unless the caller passes allow_code = TRUE. All other forms (name/ref references, class specs, named-component references) are data, not source, and are always available.
